item.title: A and an by sound at the fair
item.explanation_text:
At the community fair, the lost-item shelf has things of many colors. When you tell a helper about one thing for the first time, you can say “a cap” or “an umbrella.” Use a or an to talk about one thing you can count when you have not said which particular one.

Listen to the first sound of the word right after a or an. Use a before a consonant sound, as in “a bag.” Use an before a vowel sound, as in “an egg.” If a word that describes the thing comes first, listen to that word. Say “a blue umbrella” but “an orange cap.” Listen to the sound, even when the spelling may surprise you. Say “a uniform” because uniform starts with the same sound as yes.
item.contrast_text: Say “an umbrella” when umbrella comes right after the article. Say “a blue umbrella” when blue comes right after it. The same noun can take either article because the next sound changes.
item.common_error_pattern: Choosing a or an from the first letter alone, or listening to the noun when an adjective comes before it.

children.title: Make a shelf label
children.instructions: Complete the label for one lost item. Write only a or an.

children.title: Ask about a lost snack bag
children.instructions: Complete the visitor's question. Write only a or an.
children.prompt_text: Did anyone find ___ apple in a paper bag?

children.title: Read a note from the face-painting table
children.instructions: Complete the note about one lost item. Write only a or an.
children.prompt_text: Mia found ___ orange hat near the paints.

children.title: Describe a photo for the notice board
children.instructions: Complete the photo caption. Write only a or an.

children.title: Record what the dancers left
children.instructions: Complete the shelf record. Uniform starts with the same sound as yes. Write only a or an.
children.prompt_text: The dancers left ___ uniform by the stage.

children.title: Check the lost-item list
children.instructions: The article in this list entry is wrong. Replace it and write the whole entry.

children.title: Fix a message to a friend
children.instructions: Replace the wrong article. Keep all the other words and write the full sentence.

children.title: Add a color to a claim
children.instructions: Add green immediately before umbrella and change the article as needed. Write the full phrase.

children.title: Shorten a shelf tag
children.instructions: Remove small and change the article as needed. Write the two words for the shorter tag.

children.title: Update a description after a closer look
children.instructions: Replace new with old and change the article as needed. Write the whole sentence.

children.title: Give an item to the shelf helper
children.instructions: Use each tile once to make a sentence. Start with “Here is”.

children.title: Match a child's toy to the shelf
children.instructions: Use each tile once to make a sentence. Start with “It looks like”.
